name: zlib-ng-9e60980e-blind30
instr:
# zlib-ng: hunting thirty undocumented edits without a test suite

The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

A program that uses this library to shrink data, grow it back again and check that bytes
arrived intact now gets wrong answers across a long list of everyday situations, and
several of the command-line programs bundled with the sources are wrong as well.

Checking that bytes arrived intact goes wrong first. Asking for the rolling two-part
integrity value over a buffer of many kilobytes in one call gives a different number from
feeding the same bytes in successive chunks, and the same disagreement shows up when the
buffer is only a handful of bytes long. Asking for a duplicate of a block and its
integrity value in a single pass hands back a number unrelated to the one computed over
the copy afterwards.

The other kind of integrity value, taken over a buffer in one call, likewise disagrees
with the value for the same bytes handed in piece by piece. It disagrees for inputs only
a few bytes long, for inputs of a few kilobytes, for inputs of tens of kilobytes and for
buffers of a megabyte or more, and it disagrees as well when the bytes handed in begin
part-way into a larger allocation rather than at its start.

Shrinking data goes wrong across most of the settings a caller can pick. Input containing
long repeated runs produces a stream that expands back to something other than what went
